definition: The olfactory system is the set of sensory neurons and brain areas involved in smelling and in transmitting odor information. It can be affected by harmful agents and inflammatory signals, which may disrupt communication within this system and contribute to impaired smell function.

reasons: The definition claims the olfactory system is “involved in smelling and in transmitting odor information,” but the packet does not explicitly describe smelling/odor-information transmission in those terms; it focuses on impaired “communication between the olfactory sensory neurons and olfactory brain areas” and measured electrophysiological changes during olfactory stimulation.

The definition states that “harmful agents and inflammatory signals” can disrupt communication and contribute to impaired smell function; while the packet supports harmful agents and inflammatory molecules affecting olfactory communication and olfactory dysfunction, the definition generalizes to “inflammatory signals” and “impaired smell function” more broadly than the packet’s specific experimental context and mechanisms (e.g., IL-1β/IL-1Ra in the olfactory bulb).
